items.title: Fewer preventable hospitalizations
items.alt_text: Full practice authority for nurse practitioners. All original outcomes are retained; the acute-composite estimate is not statistically significant.
items.source: The Impact of Nurse Practitioner Scope-of-Practice Laws on Preventable Hospitalizations, Figure 3, PDF p. 10.
items.treatment: Original three-panel figure crop; original axes, outcomes, point estimates, and confidence intervals retained.

items.title: FCA sanctions rival malpractice liability
items.alt_text: Healthcare False Claims Act sanctions and medical malpractice damages over time. This is a descriptive comparison of liability, not a causal estimate.
items.source: A Constitutional False Claims Act, Figure 1, PDF p. 21.
items.treatment: Original figure crop; logarithmic scale and original units retained.

items.title: Mortality inside and outside the transplant system
items.alt_text: Estimated effects of eliminating geographic allocation boundaries: waitlist mortality minus 2.53 deaths per 1,000 waitlisted patients per month; one-year post-transplant mortality minus 1.72 percentage points; transplant-amenable mortality plus 0.61 deaths per million residents per month. Standard errors appear in parentheses in the table.
items.source: Adapted from Sharing Is Caring, Table 5, columns 2–3, PDF p. 44, and Table 7, column 1, PDF p. 45.
items.treatment: Selected reported estimates reformatted into a compact table; no new estimation.

table.caption: Estimated effects of eliminating geographic allocation boundaries
table.note: Standard errors are in parentheses; all displayed estimates have p < 0.01. The outcomes use different populations, denominators, and units and should not be added or subtracted.

items.title: Broader practice authority and lower mortality
items.alt_text: Estimated changes in annual healthcare-amenable deaths per 100,000 residents. Nurse practitioner full practice authority: minus 12.177 for all counties and minus 15.620 for rural counties. Physician assistant remote practice authority: minus 9.927 for all counties and minus 26.431 for rural counties. Standard errors appear in parentheses in the table.
items.source: Adapted from Supply-side Health Policy, Table 2, column 6, panels A–B, PDF p. 9.
items.treatment: Selected reported estimates reformatted into a compact table; no new estimation.

table.caption: Estimated changes in annual healthcare-amenable deaths per 100,000 residents
table.note: Standard errors are in parentheses. The nurse practitioner rural estimate has p < 0.05; the other displayed estimates have p < 0.01. The specification includes both practice-law variables and Medicaid expansion.

items.title: Competition and organ-allocation priority
items.alt_text: Before-and-after changes in the gap between allocation and laboratory MELD scores. Larger post-Share-35 gaps are consistent with strategic use of exception points.
items.source: Stealing Organs?, Figure 8, PDF p. 46; journal p. 180.
items.treatment: Original figure crop; baseline comparison and 95% confidence intervals retained.

items.title: Licensing and liability work together
items.alt_text: Midwife attendance and C-section use across malpractice-pressure quartiles. Differences between practice regimes narrow as malpractice pressure rises.
items.source: Healthcare Licensing and Liability, Figure 5, PDF p. 48; journal p. 867.
items.treatment: Both original panels and 90% confidence intervals retained.

items.title: NP independence and opioid prescribing
items.alt_text: All-payer estimated changes in annual morphine milligram equivalents: nurse practitioners and physicians combined minus 4.688 percent; nurse practitioners plus 4.468 percent; physicians minus 6.352 percent. P-values appear in the table.
items.source: Adapted from Nurse Practitioner Scope-of-Practice Laws and Opioid Prescribing, Table 2, PDF p. 14.
items.treatment: Selected reported percentage changes and p-values reformatted into a compact table; no new estimation.

table.caption: All-payer estimated changes in annual morphine milligram equivalents
table.note: The reported percentage changes are reproduced from the paper. The outcome is annual provider-level morphine milligram equivalents, not prescription counts.
